subject: Transient credential exposure — request for IRP, evidence transfer, and postmortem timeline
messages:
From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@finsecure.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>
Cc: ops@finsecure.com
Date: 2026-09-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Transient credential exposure observed in prefix caching

Hi Rishi,

Quick heads-up from our SRE team: during a routine telemetry sweep we saw a short-lived set of pre-signed tokens appearing in a subset of API request traces that appear to be generated by Redwood's caching layer. Tokens were valid for under 30 minutes; we believe they were cached and replayed in a rare path.

We've isolated some sample traces and attached a small JSON snapshot (finsecure_initial_alert.json) showing timestamps and redacted subjects. We're flagging this as P2 because it has measurable but limited blast radius (a narrow customer bucket).

Can you confirm receipt and share Redwood's incident response plan, an evidence transfer mechanism (SFTP or secure share), and an estimated timeline for a postmortem? Our compliance team will need artifacts mapped to SOC 2 sections and an initial containment timeline.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Harper
Head of Infrastructure, FinSecure
ops@finsecure.com

Date: 2026-09-17T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient credential exposure observed in prefix caching

Alex — thanks for the report and the sample. Confirming receipt.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Rotated the affected short-lived signing tokens and invalidated the cache slices implicated.
- Throttled the serving pool to force a cold path for any cached prefixes while we triage.
- Preserved runtime telemetry, KV cache snapshots, and audit logs — we will provide a sanitized evidence bundle.

What we need from you to expedite transfer:
1) Preferred secure transfer method (SFTP endpoint or pre-authorized secure share).
2) Any specific PII redaction constraints beyond what you've already applied.
3) The SOC 2 sections your compliance team wants explicitly mapped (if unknown we'll include a standard mapping for CC6, CC7, CC8).

Proposed timeline:
- 24 hours: secure evidence handoff (sanitized log extracts, cache snapshots)
- 72 hours: forensic summary and containment write-up
- 5 business days: full postmortem draft and remediation plan

I'm looping in Marissa (forensics lead), Jonas (platform engineering), and Neha (compliance) on next steps.

For evidence handling, please use our secure share: https://redwood-secure-share.example/finsecure/20260919 — we will upload the bundle there after confirmation. Attached is a short preservation note with exact log extract commands.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security and Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Transient credential exposure — postmortem and artifacts delivered

Alex — attaching the postmortem and final artifact index. Thank you and your team for the quick signal. Below is an executive summary; the full postmortem is attached.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2026-09-17T06:50:00Z to 2026-09-17T07:20:00Z (replayable window observed from traces).
- Root cause: race condition in prefix-cache eviction logic that, under a specific concurrency pattern, associated a recently issued short-lived signing token with a different request context. This resulted in a small number of requests containing a token that was valid for <30 minutes.
- Impact: limited to a single FinSecure customer bucket; we identified ~14 anomalous request traces matching the pattern. No downstream token exchange or external exfiltration detected.
- Containment: rotated signing keys, forced cache cold-start for impacted pool, added rate-limiting guard for prefix-cache writes.
- Remediation (short term): backported a patch to prevent token association on cache miss, added stricter atomic checks during token issuance.
- Remediation (long term): redesign prefix cache to separate token lifecycle from request contexts and add end-to-end tests for concurrent issuance patterns.

Artifacts delivered: redwood_postmortem_finsecure_20260923.pdf, audit-log-extract-20260917-19.csv, evidence_bundle_finsecure_20260919.zip

Compliance mapping: our postmortem includes a SOC 2 mapping appendix (CC6.1, CC7.2, CC8.3) and a SIG/CAIQ crosswalk; if your compliance team wants a bespoke mapping we can schedule a short working session.

Please reply to confirm receipt of the attachments and the secure share. If you need any additional redactions or extended retention for audit, we can accommodate.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security and Compliance
Redwood Inference
